model: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct BF16, identical nine-worker binary 506b3e2519dd3c3dbb35c05f966b0fab339ae3326c5ecf21b0e8c118c1a015d6 on two leased A100s, max active 8, waiting 2, HTTP loopback
design: Preload a 5745-token prompt in a new private Router on the busy replica. 8 independent 384-token streams on that replica, one real 3-turn source-checked agent on the other replica. Once that agent's final answer and all incumbent streams are visible release 0, 16, 64 or 160 one-shot calls onto the first replica. At +650ms route the repeated prompt. Incumbents and burst bypass the router and share no local counters with it. No retries. Reverse GPU roles, wave order and policy order for the second block. Use a fresh early tag each time. Report failures without retry or exclusion.
comparison: observed-capacity includes replicas with unknown current load and falls back to local counters. fresh-capacity prefers a verified open replica if one exists and otherwise preserves the previous fallback. Same readiness sampler, both policies.
gates: Every targeted continuation must succeed with one content token, all eight incumbents must overlap the decision and burst release, real protected final content must span release, and the protected 3-turn agent must validate. Report head-of-line delay to first and final content. At nonzero bursts with unknown busy load require routing to the available peer, successful continuation and a lower TTFT than paired control when control chose busy. At zero burst require both policies to select the available peer. For each matched cell protect the other agent's final-content gap p95, final completion and incumbent pooled p95 gap within 5%. Report every error, refusals and transport failures, poll outcomes, sample age and recovery. Insufficient samples cannot establish fleet-wide performance.
